label: CORRECTION of f-iter006-004: sync-phase-map-status.ts loads and parses arguments under npx tsx (unknown argument: --help, EXIT=1) and fails only under plain node type-stripping with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND for ../lib/esm-entry.js (EXIT=1); the runtime README never documents an invocation for the file at all (tree line and table row only), so the original claim of a documented invocation that exits 1 is unsupported. What survives is narrower: the file is the only .ts under runtime/cli/spec with no shebang while its two tsx-run siblings declare #!/usr/bin/env npx tsx, so a reader who reaches for node gets a resolution crash with no hint that tsx is required.

The speckit index carries three mutually inconsistent inventories: 7 command .md files on disk, a self-count at README.txt:116 that says 9-command index, a COMMANDS table at :67 with 10 rows because it mixes two /deep commands and a plan --intake-only variant into the speckit family, and a structure tree that closes the assets branch at :132 after drawing 8 of the 12 files on disk, omitting speckit-complete/implement/plan/resume-presentation.txt even though :148 explains the prefix convention those four files follow. f-iter006-002's table-lists-ten is confirmed but the 7-vs-9 gap and the stale tree are new.

validate.sh and create.sh disagree on the --level flag: validate.sh has no such option and answers a guess with ERROR: Unknown option '--level' EXIT=1 with no list of valid flags though its --help prints one, while create.sh one directory away accepts --level and on a bad value enumerates all seven accepted values with EXIT=1 but does not advertise the flag in its own usage line. An operator who learns the vocabulary from one CLI gets an inert rejection from the other.

Exit codes 1 and 2 carry incompatible meanings across the spec-kit front doors: validate.sh uses 1 for unknown option and missing argument but 3 for a folder that does not exist; create.sh uses 1 for both no-arguments and a bad level; lookup-trigger-index.mjs uses 2 for an unknown argument but 1 for a clean no-hit while still printing a complete schema-versioned JSON envelope; check-goal.cjs uses 2 for conformance errors. A wrapper written as cmd && next or set -e cannot separate usage error from empty result from invalid artifact.

A write-verb-first rule for the Gate 3 classifier: nineteen bare write tokens are collected at gate-3-classifier.ts:151 and the read-only cancel is decided only after aggregation, by positional helpers at :833 and inside the mixed-tail check, so clause order participates in the outcome without being named in the contract. Proposal: compute the first write verb in the imperative head (before the first comma/and/then/newline) and let it veto the read-only override, plus an order-invariance golden test that reverses clause order for every existing golden prompt.

No validate rule scans a phase parent's required anchors: check-spec-doc-integrity.sh contains zero occurrences of phase, parent, ANCHOR or required, so anchor enforcement is per-document and nothing reads the parent's Phase Documentation Map, while the only tool that would correct that map is the uncalled sync-phase-map-status. Proposal: add and register check-phase-anchors.sh asserting each phase child carries its level's anchor set and each child has exactly one row in the parent map, feature-detected from folder grammar.

check-goal collapses warnings into success and leaves exit 1 unused: its only numeric return is 2 for conformance errors and its top-level catch also sets 2, so an over-budget or advisory goal exits 0 and a hook cannot gate on warning severity without parsing stdout. Proposal: a three-value contract 0 clean / 1 warnings-only / 2 errors with one fixture per code, which also gives the goal checker the only code the rest of the family does not already use.

sk-code's TypeScript standard requires every file to begin with a module header and exempts only emitted .d.ts files, but a sweep of 115 non-test .ts files under runtime/cli found 14 whose first non-blank line is a shebang instead, all of them executable entry points whose line 1 must be a shebang for the kernel to honour it. The gap is in the standard rather than the code: amending the rule to begin with a module header after an optional shebang line turns 14 silent violations into 14 conforming files with no code change.

sk-code's TypeScript references state no test-placement rule at all, only a .d.ts co-location rule, while system-spec-kit's own vitest run reports three distinct project prefixes for suites in one package (cli:tests/, bare :tests/, root:../tests/), so a reviewer has no rule to cite for which root is canonical and the same skill keeps tests in at least three places. Proposal: add a placement rule naming one root per package, enforced by the existing test-layout check.

system-spec-kit SKILL.md conforms to sk-doc's required section order WHEN TO USE, SMART ROUTING, HOW IT WORKS, RULES and REFERENCES, with SUCCESS CRITERIA and INTEGRATION POINTS inserted before the closing section in a way that preserves the canon's relative order; the only drift is the heading name, REFERENCES AND RELATED RESOURCES where the canon says REFERENCES, which is the one place a canon citation would fail to resolve by grep.

Measured exit-code matrix: validate.sh --nope=1, missing folder=3, --level 99=1, --help=0; create.sh no-args=1, --level 9=1; lookup-trigger-index.mjs --bogus-flag=2, valid no-hit=1 with JSON; plain node on the sync script=1 with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND; npx tsx same file=1 from the argument parser.
Disk recount: 7 speckit command .md files, 12 asset files, README self-count 9, COMMANDS table 10 rows (2 deep + 1 plan variant), structure tree draws 8 assets.

A standard that a conforming artifact cannot satisfy literally is wrong, not the artifact: a shebang must occupy line 1, so a module-header rule that exempts only emitted declaration files makes every executable TypeScript entry point non-conforming by construction.
A nonzero exit code is a contract shared by every caller, so two tools in one family must not assign the same code to usage error, empty result and invalid artifact.

direction: Treating f-iter006-004 as a broken script that needs a code fix
reason: Both runners were probed: tsx reaches the argument parser, plain node fails only at import resolution. The defect is an undocumented runner and a missing shebang, not a defective module.
